On October 6, 2026, the board of directors (the “Board”) of Aardvark Therapeutics, Inc. (the “Company”) appointed David (Zhongwei) Zhang, Ph.D., MBA, as a Class II director of the Company, effective October 7, 2026. Dr. Zhang, age 58, has over 25 years of experience designing clinical programs, analyzing pivotal trial data and supporting regulatory submissions. He has served as the Chief Strategy Officer of Abivax S.A., a clinical-stage biotechnology company focused on therapeutics for chronic inflammatory diseases, since July 2024. At Abivax S.A., he is a member of the Executive Committee and has overseen biometrics, regulatory affairs, quality assurance and health economics and outcomes research. At Abivax S.A., he led the biometrics team through positive topline readouts of two pivotal Phase 3 trials of obefazimod in ulcerative colitis. Previously, from March 2021 to July 2024, Dr. Zhang was Senior Vice President, Head of Biometrics and Data Management at Alumis Inc., where, as a founding executive, he built the biometrics and data management functions, served as interim Chief Information Officer, and helped the company progress through its initial public offering. Before joining Alumis Inc., Dr. Zhang was Vice President, Head of Biometrics, Data Science and Digital Health at MyoKardia, Inc., where he oversaw the pivotal trial design, readout and New Drug Application submission for CAMZYOS® (mavacamten) for treating obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy prior to the company’s acquisition by Bristol Myers Squibb in 2020. Earlier in his career, Dr. Zhang held biometrics and strategic innovation leadership roles at Roche Sequencing Solutions and Genentech/Roche over a 15 year period, and statistician roles at Eli Lilly and Company and Abbott Laboratories. Dr. Zhang has served on the board of directors of the Bay Area Biotech-Pharma Statistics Workshop and is a past president of the organization. He holds a Ph.D. in biostatistics from the UCLA Fielding School of Public Health and an executive MBA in finance from the Kelley School of Business at Indiana University, and completed postdoctoral research in statistical genetics at Columbia University. In accordance with the Company’s Non-Employee Director Compensation Program (the “Program”), as a non-employee director of the Company, Dr. Zhang is entitled to receive cash compensation in the amount of $40,000 per year for his service on the Board, prorated for the portion of the year during which he serves on the Board. In addition, pursuant to the Program, on October 7, 2026, Dr. Zhang was granted an option with respect to such number of shares of the Company’s common stock as is equal to $500,000, divided by the per share grant date fair value of the option award (the “Appointment Option”)

At the initial closing, the Company issued an aggregate of 380,232 Ordinary Shares and Ordinary Warrants to purchase up to 380,232 Ordinary Shares. Pursuant to the Securities Purchase Agreement, the Investors have also irrevocably committed, subject only to the continued listing of the Ordinary Shares on Nasdaq or another U.S. national securities exchange, to purchase an additional $7.0 million of Ordinary Shares (or Pre-Funded Warrants in lieu thereof) and accompanying Ordinary Warrants at the same price in 10 monthly closings of $0.7 million each, scheduled to occur from December 1, 2026 through September 1, 2027. Certain of the subsequent closings may be postponed until the Company’s receipt of shareholder approval of an increase in its authorized share capital, and any subsequent closing may be postponed if the Registration Statement is not then available. The Ordinary Warrants have an exercise price of $1.578 per Ordinary Share, are immediately exercisable and will expire three years following the initial closing date, including Ordinary Warrants issued at the subsequent closings. Each Pre-Funded Warrant has an exercise price of $0.001 per Ordinary Share, is immediately exercisable and may be exercised at any time and has no expiration date. The Ordinary Warrants and the Pre-Funded Warrants are subject to customary adjustments; however, no such warrants contain any “ratchet” or other financial antidilution provisions. None of the Warrants may be exercised if the aggregate number of Ordinary Shares beneficially owned by the holder thereof, together with its affiliates and any person acting as a group with the holder or its affiliates, would exceed 19.99% immediately after exercise thereof. The Offering was made directly by the Company, without a placement agent, underwriter, broker or dealer, and no placement agent fees are payable. The initial closing of the Offering occurred on November 17, 2026. The gross proceeds from the initial closing of the Offering were approximately $0.5 million, and the aggregate gross proceeds from the Offering, assuming all subsequent closings are completed, will be approximately $7.5 million, in each case before deducting estimated expenses relating to the Offering and excluding any proceeds from the exercise of the Ordinary Warrants. Form 20-F ☒ Form 40-F ☐ Securities Purchase Agreement On November 14, 2026, Enlivex Ltd., a company organized under the laws of the State of Israel (the “ Company ”), entered into a securities purchase agreement (the “ Securities Purchase Agreement ”) with certain investors (the “ Investors ”), for the purchase and sale, in a registered direct offering, of an aggregate of $7,500,000 of ordinary shares, par value NIS 96.00 per share, of the Company (the “ Ordinary Shares ” and, such Ordinary Shares offered in the Registered Offering, the “ Shares ”) (or pre-funded warrants in lieu thereof to purchase Ordinary Shares (the “ Pre-Funded Warrants ”)), together with accompanying ordinary warrants to purchase up to an equal number of Ordinary Shares (the “ Ordinary Warrants ” and, together with the Shares and the Pre-Funded Warrants, the “ Securities ”), at a combined purchase price of $1.315 per Share (or $1.314 per Pre-Funded Warrant) and accompanying Ordinary Warrant, representing a premium of 10.5% to the Nasdaq official closing price of the Ordinary Shares on November 13, 2026 (the “ Registered Offering ”). The Ordinary Warrants will have an exercise price of $1.578 per Ordinary Share, will be exercisable immediately upon issuance and will expire three years from the initial closing date. The Pre-Funded Warrants will have an exercise price of $0.001 per Ordinary Share, will be exercisable immediately upon issuance and will not expire until exercised in full. To the extent that an Investor (together with its affiliates and any person acting as a group with such Investor or its affiliates) would beneficially own in excess of 19.99% of the Ordinary Shares outstanding immediately after giving effect to the issuance of Shares at any closing, such Investor will purchase Pre-Funded Warrants in lieu of the Shares that would result in such excess. The Registered Offering will be consummated in a series of closings. At the initial closing, which is expected to occur on or about November 17, 2026, subject to the satisfaction of customary closing conditions, the Investors will purchase an aggregate of $500,000 of Securities. The Investors have also irrevocably committed, subject only to the continued listing of the Ordinary Shares on Nasdaq or another U.S. national securities exchange, to purchase an additional aggregate $700,000 of Securities at each of 10 subsequent monthly closings, commencing on December 1, 2026 and ending on or about September 1, 2027, for an aggregate of $7,000,000, at the same price and on the same terms as those applicable to the initial closing. Certain of the subsequent closings may be postponed until the Company’s receipt of shareholder approval of an increase in its authorized share capital, and any subsequent closing may be postponed if the Company’s registration statement or prospectus is not then available. The purchase price may be paid in U.S. dollars, Tether (USDT) or a combination thereof. The aggregate gross proceeds to the Company from the Registered Offering are expected to be approximately $7.5 million, assuming all closings are consummated, before deducting offering expenses payable by the Company and excluding any proceeds from the exercise of the Ordinary Warrants. The Shares, Pre-Funded Warrants and Ordinary Warrants offered in the Registered Offering, and the Ordinary Shares issuable upon exercise of such warrants, are being offered by the Company pursuant to a shelf registration statement on Form F-3 (File No. 333-286956 ) previously filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the “ SEC ”), which became effective on May 12, 2025. Such Appeal hearing request will result in a stay of any suspension or delisting action pending the Appeal hearing, during which time the ordinary shares will continue to trade on the Nasdaq Capital Market. The Company cannot provide assurances that the Appeal will ultimately be successful and that its ordinary shares will continue to trade on the Nasdaq Capital Market following the hearing. Item 2.05. Costs Associated with Exit or Disposal Activities. On November 4, 2026, the board of directors of Eos Energy Enterprises, Inc.(“we”, “the Company” or “Eos”) adopted a plan that is intended to better align cost structure and support gross margin improvement to the Company’s target financial model, while also aligning manufacturing capabilities with current and anticipated business needs and the Company's strategic priorities. As part of this plan, the Company is consolidating the manufacturing facilities located in Turtle Creek, Pennsylvania and Thorn Hill, Pennsylvania. We expect the actions defined under this plan will be largely completed by the end of June 2027 with the production line anticipated to be operational within the first quarter 2027. The plan is expected to result in the Company recording cash restructuring charges in the aggregate amount of approximately $16 to $18 million on a GAAP basis, estimated to be comprised primarily of costs relating to moving and clean up. This Current Report on Form 8-K contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. These statements are based on the Company’s current expectations and are subject to significant risks and uncertainties. Potential Adverse Effects - Dilution and Impact on Existing Stockholders The issuance of shares of Common Stock upon the Conversion will have a dilutive effect on current stockholders in that the percentage ownership of the Company held by such current stockholders will decline as a result of the issuance of the shares of Common Stock issuable upon the conversion. (Exact Name of Registrant as Specified in its Charter) No. 190 Xizhang Road, Gushan Town, Jiangyin City, Jiangsu Province People’s Republic of China +86 0510-81630030 (Address of principal executive offices) Indicate by check mark whether the registrant files or will file annual reports under cover of Form 20-F or Form 40-F: Form 20-F ☒ Form 40-F ☐ Entry into a Material Definitive Agreement On November 3, 2026, Jiangsu Libang Intelligent Technology Co., Ltd. (the “ Buyer ”), a limited liability company incorporated in the People’s Republic of China and a wholly-owned subsidiary of Li Bang International Corporation Inc., a Cayman Islands exempted company with limited liability (the “ Company ”), entered into a Share Purchase Agreement (the “ Agreement ”) with respect to the acquisition of the controlling equity interest in Jiangsu Xinsheng Synthetic Materials Co., Ltd., a limited liability company incorporated in the People’s Republic of China (the “ Target Company ”). The Target Company is a supplier of innovative and high-performance chemical raw materials and a provider of professional technical support services for applications of such chemical raw materials. The parties to the Agreement are the Company, the Buyer, the Target Company and the two individual shareholders of the Target Company collectively owning 100% equity interest in the Target Company (collectively, the “ Sellers ”). Pursuant to the Agreement, the Buyer agreed to purchase from the Sellers an aggregate of fifty point one percent (50.1%) of the issued and outstanding equity interest of the Target Company (the “ Subject Equity ”) for an aggregate purchase price consisting of (i) 2,000,000 Class A ordinary shares of the Company (the “ Consideration Shares ”) to be issued by the Company and (ii) cash consideration in the amount of US$23,000,000, to be paid in three installments. The transactions contemplated by the Agreement are to be implemented in three successive stages: a first closing (the “ First Closing ”), a second closing and a third closing. On the date of the First Closing, which is to occur on or before the tenth (10th) business day following the signing of the Agreement, the Company is to issue the Consideration Shares and pay the first installment of the cash consideration of US$3,000,000. The transfer of the Subject Equity and payment of the remaining cash installments are to occur at the subsequent closings, in each case subject to and in accordance with the terms and conditions of the Agreement. The Consideration Shares are subject to lock-up restrictions and a performance-based leak-out schedule as set forth in the Agreement. The Company has agreed to a reverse split top-up mechanism intended to preserve the Sellers an aggregate of 2,000,000 Consideration Shares during a protection period commencing on the date of the First Closing and ending on the third (3rd) anniversary thereof. If, at any time during that protection period, the Company effects any reverse stock split, share consolidation or other similar combination of its shares that reduces the aggregate number of Consideration Shares then held by the Sellers, the Company shall issue to the Sellers such additional shares as are necessary (the “ Supplemental Shares ”) so that the aggregate number of Consideration Shares and Supplemental Shares held by the Sellers equals 2,000,000. Any Supplemental Shares issued will be treated as Consideration Shares for all purposes of the Agreement and will be subject to the same lock-up restrictions and performance-based leak-out schedule. The Company anticipates that the First Closing will take place in accordance with the terms of the Agreement. Principal Effects of the Blank Check Amendment If the May 2026 Notes are converted into shares of Series A Preferred Stock, the issuance of such shares could adversely affect the holders of our common stock. See “—The Series A Preferred Stock,” below for a discussion of the powers, designations, preferences, limitations, restrictions and rights of the Series A Preferred Stock and how the issuance of such shares could adversely affect the holders of our common stock. In addition, the Board will be permitted, potentially without future stockholder approval, to issue shares of other series of preferred stock with dividend, liquidation, conversion, voting and other rights, powers or preferences that are superior to the rights, powers and preferences of our common stock and may adversely affect the holders of our common stock. These rights, powers or preferences could, for example, result in a series of preferred stock ranking senior to our common stock in respect of dividends and in the event of a liquidation, dissolution or other winding up of the Company, reduce the amount of funds, if any, available for distribution to the holders of our common stock, including in connection with an acquisition of the Company, and dilute the voting power of the holders of our common stock. The holders of preferred stock may be entitled to receive a certain amount of dividends per share before the holders of our common stock receive any dividend or other distribution, to vote as a separate class on specified matters, including the election of directors, and/or to vote with the holders of our common stock as a single class, which would dilute the voting power of the holders of our common stock. The issuance of preferred stock would decrease existing stockholders’ percentage equity ownership, dilute any earnings per share and book value per share of our common stock, and, depending upon the price at which they are issued, could be dilutive to existing stockholders. In addition, the future issuance of shares of our preferred stock or securities convertible or exercisable into shares of our preferred stock could adversely affect the trading price of our common stock, including if, for example, shares of preferred stock are issued and sold at prices below the then-current trading price of our common stock, or, if the preferred stock is convertible into our common stock and the conversion price is below the then-current trading price of our common stock. For additional effects of stockholder approval of the Blank Check Amendment, see “—Potential Anti-Takeover Effects,” below. Beneficial Ownership Limitation . We may not effect any conversion of the Series A Preferred Stock, and a holder will not have the right to convert any portion of their Series A Preferred Stock, to the extent that after giving effect to such conversion, such holder would beneficially own in excess of 9.99% of the number of shares of our common stock outstanding immediately after giving effect to the issuance of shares of common stock issuable upon conversion of the Series A Preferred Stock held by the applicable holder, together with its affiliates. Dividends . Beginning six months from the date of issuance, the Series A Preferred Stock will accrue dividends equal to 10% of the stated value over each subsequent twelve-month per

thly basis and being added to the stated value. Redemption . We will have no right to redeem the Series A Preferred Stock. Voting Rights . Except as otherwise required by law, the Series A Preferred Stock will have one vote per share and, except as described in the next sentence, will vote with the common stock as a single class. As long as any shares of Series A Preferred Stock are outstanding, we cannot, without the affirmative vote of the holders of all the then outstanding shares of the Series A Preferred Stock, (a) alter or change adversely the powers, preferences or rights given to the Series A Pref

tion Rights . Upon our liquidation, dissolution or winding-up, the holders of Series A Preferred Stock will be entitled to receive out of our assets, for each share of Series A Preferred Stock, an amount equal to the greater of (i) the stated value of such share and (ii) the amount that a holder of common stock would receive if such shares of Series A Preferred Stock were fully converted (disregarding for such purposes any conversion limitations hereunder) into common stock. Preemption Rights . None. Subsequent Rights Offerings . If at any time we grant, issue or sell any common stock equivalents or rights to purchase stock, warrants, securities or other property on a pro rata basis to the record holders of our common stock (collectively, “Purchase Rights”), each holder of Series A Preferred Stock will be entitled to acquire, upon the same terms applicable to such Purchase Rights, the aggregate Purchase Rights that such holder could have acquired if it had held the number of shares of common stock acquirable upon complete conversion of its Series A Preferred Stock immediately prior to the applicable record date for the grant, issuance or sale of such Purchase Rights, without regard to any limitations on conversion. Distribution Rights . Holders of the Series A Preferred Stock will be entitled to participate on an as-converted basis in any dividend or other distribution of our assets (or rights to acquire its assets) made to holders of our common stock (each, a “Distribution”). Participation rights will be calculated based on the number of shares of common stock that would be acquirable upon complete conversion of the holder’s Series A Preferred Stock immediately prior to the applicable record date for such Distribution, without regard to any limitations on conversion of the Series A Preferred Stock. Fundamental Transactions . If, at any time while any shares of Series A Preferred Stock are outstanding, we consummate a fundamental transaction (as such term is described in the certificate of designation for the Series A Preferred Stock, which generally includes any reorganization, recapitalization or reclassification of our common stock, the sale, transfer or other disposition of all or substantially all of our properties or assets, our consolidation or merger with or into another person, the acquisition of more than 50% of our outstanding common stock, or any person or group becoming the beneficial owner of 50% of the voting power represented by our outstanding common stock), then upon any subsequent conversion of Series A Preferred Stock, each holder will be entitled to receive, in lieu of shares of our common stock, the kind and amount of securities, cash or other property that such holder would have received had it converted its Series A Preferred Stock immediately prior to such fundamental transaction, determined without regard to any limitations on conversion. - 7 - Potential Dilution The following tables illustrate the approximate number of shares of common stock that would be issued, and the resulting dilution to our existing stockholders, at various assumed conversion prices of the May 2026 Notes, in each case based on the 4,515,862 shares of our common stock outstanding as of September 28, 2026 (the “Measurement Date”). The 20% Approval The Company’s common stock is listed on the Nasdaq Capital Market and, as such, the Company is subject to the Nasdaq Listing Rules. Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(d) requires stockholder approval prior to the issuance of securities in connection with a transaction, other than a public offering, involving the sale, issuance or potential issuance by the Company of common stock (or securities convertible into or exercisable for common stock), which alone or together with sales by officers, directors or substantial stockholders of the company, equals 20% or more of the common stock or 20% or more of the voting power outstanding before the issuance, in each case, at a price that is less than the Minimum Price. The “Minimum Price” is generally defined as the lower of (1) the Nasdaq official closing price (as reflected on Nasdaq.com) immediately preceding the signing of the binding agreement or (2) the average Nasdaq official closing price of the common stock (as reflected on Nasdaq.com) for the five trading days immediately preceding the signing of the binding agreement. These retainers are paid quarterly in arrears on or before the fifteenth (15th) business day following the end of each calendar quarter. Each non-employee director also receives an annual equity award of 60,000 shares of common stock under the Company’s Amended and Restated 2023 Equity Incentive Plan. Upon appointment, each non-employee directors will receive 200,000 restricted shares of common stock, vesting in equal instalments over three (3) years. On November 16, 2026, the Company filed a Certificate of Amendment to the Company’s Amended and Restated Certificate of Incorporation, as amended, with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware (the “Certificate of Amendment”), which became effective at 4:00 p.m. Eastern Time on November 16, 2026, and implemented a one-for-seven (1:7) reverse stock split (the “Reverse Stock Split”) of the Company’s issued and outstanding shares of Class A Common Stock, each with a par value $0.00001 per share (together, the “Common Stock”). In connection with the Reverse Stock Split, the CUSIP number for the Common Stock changed to 60743G308. The trading symbol for the Common Stock remains “MOBX”. As a result of the Reverse Stock Split, every seven (7) shares of Common Stock issued and outstanding were converted into one (1) share of Common Stock. No fractional shares will be issued in connection with the Reverse Stock Split. Any fractional shares of Common Stock resulting from the Reverse Stock Split will instead be rounded up to the nearest whole share. The Reverse Stock Split affects all stockholders uniformly and does not alter any stockholder’s percentage ownership interest in the Company, except for adjustments related to fractional shares. The Reverse Stock Split will also proportionately adjust the number of shares available under the Company’s equity incentive plan and the exercise price and number of shares underlying stock options and warrants outstanding on the day the Reverse Stock Split was effective, in each case in accordance with their terms. The Reverse Stock Split did not change the par value of the Common Stock or the authorized number of shares of Common Stock. Additionally, the Company has instructed Continental Stock Transfer and Trust Company (“Continental”) to send a notice to the holders of the Company’s outstanding: (i) public warrants to purchase up to 85,715 shares of Class A Common Stock; and (ii) private placement warrants to purchase up to 48,572 shares of common stock (the “Private Placement Warrants”), in each case, pursuant to that certain Warrant Agreement between Chavant Capital Acquisition Corporation and Continental, as warrant agent, dated December 21, 2023, informing the holders that, as a result of the Reverse Stock Split, each Public Warrant and Private Placement Warrant will become exercisable for 1/7 th of a share of common stock at an exercise price of $405.30 per share. Why We Seek Stockholder Approval for a Reverse Stock Split? The Board believes that providing authority to implement one or more reverse stock splits, in its sole discretion, is in the best interests of the Company and its stockholders. On July 10, 2025, the Company received a notice from The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC (“Nasdaq”) indicating that the bid price of the Company’s Class A Common Stock had closed below the minimum $1.00 per share requirement for continued listing on The Nasdaq Capital Market under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5550(a)(2). Following implementation of the reverse stock split authority previously approved by stockholders, the Company regained compliance with the minimum bid price requirement. On May 11, 2026, the Company received written notice from Nasdaq confirming that it had regained compliance, and the matter was closed. As described in our Definitive Information Statement on Schedule 14C filed with the SEC on November 4, 2025, holders of a majority of the voting power of our Common Stock approved, by written consent dated October 19, 2025, authority for the Board to effect one or more reverse stock splits at a ratio between 1 -for-2 and 1 -for-100 on or before 5 Table of Contents June 30, 2026. Under that authority, the Board effected a 1 -for-10 reverse stock split that became effective on April 24, 2026 and, following Board approval on June 26, 2026, a 1 -for-5 reverse stock split that became effective on July 22, 2026, as described in our Current Reports on Form 8 -K filed on April 22, 2026 and July 20, 2026. That authority has expired, and the Board has no authority to effect a further reverse stock split without the approval of our stockholders. Under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5810(c)(3)(A)(iv), if a company’s security fails to meet the minimum bid price requirement and the company has effected a reverse stock split over the prior one -year period, or has effected one or more reverse stock splits over the prior two -year period with a cumulative ratio of 250 shares or more to one, the company is not eligible for any compliance period and Nasdaq will issue a Staff Delisting Determination with respect to that security. Because we effected reverse stock splits in April 2026 and July 2026, if the closing bid price of our Class A Common Stock were to fall below $1.00 per share for 30 consecutive business days before July 22, 2027, we would not be eligible for a compliance period. Effects of a Reverse Stock Split A Reverse Stock Split refers to a reduction in the number of outstanding shares of the Company’s Class A Common Stock and Class B Common Stock by reclassifying and combining such shares into a proportionately smaller number of shares. For example, a stockholder holding 100,000 shares of Class A Common Stock before the Reverse Stock Split would instead hold 1,000 shares of Class A Common Stock immediately following a 1 -for-100 Reverse Stock Split. Similarly, a stockholder holding 10,000 shares of Class B Common Stock immediately prior to the Reverse Stock Split would instead hold 100 shares of Class B Common Stock immediately following such Reverse Stock Split. All shares of Class A Common Stock and Class B Common Stock will remain validly issued, fully paid and non -assessable . Upon the effectiveness of the Reverse Stock Split, each two (2) to one hundred (100) shares of the Company’s Common Stock, depending on the Reverse Stock Split ratio selected by the Board, will automatically be combined into one (1) new share of Common Stock without any action by the Company or its stockholders. No fractional shares of Common Stock will be issued. Any fractional shares resulting from the Reverse Stock Split will be rounded up to the nearest whole share. The Reverse Stock Split will also result in proportionate adjustments to the number of shares issuable upon the exercise, conversion or exchange of the Company’s outstanding warrants, options and other convertible securities, if any, as well as to the applicable exercise or conversion prices thereof, in accordance with the terms of such securities. If the results of the Company’s due diligence differ materially from information provided by BitRock, the pre-money valuation is to be adjusted, and either party may request an independent valuation. The investment proceeds are to be used solely for construction of the Project. The instalments and disbursement conditions will be set out in a definitive investment agreement (the “Definitive Agreement”). BitRock would be responsible for construction management and day-to-day operations of the Project. As a shareholder, the Company would have the right to appoint directors, receive periodic financial reports and participate in decisions on major matters, as further set out in the Definitive Agreement. BitRock has represented that certain customers have entered into memoranda of understanding with BitRock for hosting services. This information has not been independently verified by the Company and is subject to the Company’s due diligence. BitRock has also estimated that the Project’s hosting revenue will have a net profit margin of approximately 25% to 30%, which estimate has not been independently verified by the Company and is subject to the Company’s due diligence. The LOI is legally binding upon execution, and the parties have agreed to execute the Definitive Agreement in good faith as soon as practicable on the terms of the LOI. That authorization was fully consumed when the Board effected a 1-for-30 reverse stock split of the Company’s Common Stock, effective July 6, 2026. The Board is now asking shareholders to approve a new authorization to effect one or more reverse stock splits during the one-year period following shareholder approval. The proposed amendment would authorize the Board, in its discretion, to effect one or more reverse stock splits at ratios ranging from not less than one-for-five (1:5) to not greater than one-for-one-hundred (1:100) during the authorization period. The Board could select the timing and ratio of each split, provided that the cumulative ratio of all reverse stock splits effected under this authorization does not exceed one-for-one-hundred (1:100). Purpose of the Reverse Stock Split The primary purpose of the proposed reverse stock split authorization is to increase the per-share trading price of our Common Stock to help the Company maintain compliance with the Nasdaq Capital Market’s continued listing requirements, including the minimum bid-price requirement under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5550(a)(2). The Board believes that retaining the ability to effect a reverse stock split during the authorization period would provide flexibility to respond to market conditions and any future listing deficiency. Implementation and Effect of the Reverse Stock Split If shareholders approve this proposal, the Board may select one or more ratios and effective dates within the approved range and may elect not to proceed with any split. Recommendation of the Board of Directors OUR BOARD OF DIRECTORS UNANIMOUSLY RECOMMENDS THAT SHAREHOLDERS VOTE “FOR” APPROVAL OF THE REVERSE STOCK SPLIT AUTHORIZATION UNDER PROPOSAL No. 6. 31 PROPOSAL No. 7: APPROVAL, FOR PURPOSES OF COMPLYING WITH NASDAQ LISTING RULE 5635(d), OF THE POTENTIAL ISSUANCE OF SHARES OF COMMON STOCK PURSUANT TO THE EQUITY PURCHASE FACILITY AGREEMENT On May 22, 2026, we entered into an Equity Purchase Facility Agreement (the “EPFA”) with an institutional investor (the “Investor”), pursuant to which the Company has the right, but not the obligation, to issue and sell to the Investor, from time to time during a 24-month commitment period, up to $100,000,000 in aggregate amount of newly issued shares of Common Stock, subject to the terms and conditions set forth therein. Subject to the terms and conditions of the EPFA, the Company, in its sole discretion, may from time to time deliver an advance notice directing the Investor to purchase a specified amount of shares of Common Stock (the “Advance Shares”) at certain agreed upon pricing mechanisms based on the volume weighted average price of our Common Stock during applicable pricing periods, subject to a discount. There are no mandatory minimum amounts for each advance or non-usage fees for not initiating advances. The EPFA contains certain limitations on advances, including (i) a beneficial ownership limitation restricting the Investor from owning more than 4.99% (or 9.99% upon election) of our outstanding Common Stock, (ii) unless and until we obtain stockholder approval, an exchange cap limiting issuances to 19.99% of the outstanding Common Stock as of the date of the EPFA (the “Exchange Cap”), and (iii) a registration limitation providing that no advance may exceed the amount registered under the then-effective registration statement. Under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(d), shareholder approval is required before the issuance of Common Stock (or securities convertible into Common Stock) equal to 20% or more of the pre-transaction outstanding shares at a price below the Nasdaq Minimum Price. Because the purchase price of the Advance Shares under the EPFA may result in issuances at a price below the Nasdaq Minimum Price, and because the number of shares issuable may equal or exceed 20% of our currently outstanding Common Stock, we are seeking shareholder approval to permit such issuances in compliance with Nasdaq rules and to remove the Exchange Cap. If shareholders approve this proposal, we will be authorized to issue Advance Shares in accordance with the terms of the EPFA in excess of 19.99% of our outstanding Common Stock as of the date of the EPFA, even if the purchase price is below the Nasdaq Minimum Price. Approval will not, by itself, result in any immediate issuance of shares. If shareholder approval is not obtained, issuances in excess of 19.99% of the issued and outstanding shares of Common Stock as of May 22, 2026 will not be permitted under the EPFA, which could limit our ability to access the full $100,000,000 commitment amount and restrict our future financing flexibility. her general corporate purposes. Appointment of President Effective November 12, 2026, the board of directors (the “Board”) of T1 Energy Inc. (the “Company”) appointed Evan Calio, 59, the Company’s current Chief Financial Officer, as the Company’s President. Mr. Calio will continue in his position as the Company’s Chief Financial Officer. The compensatory and other material terms of Mr. Calio’s employment agreement, dated June 3, 2024, will remain unchanged except as revised to reflect Mr. Calio’s new title of President and Chief Financial Officer. Mr. Calio has served as the Company’s Chief Financial Officer since June 2024. Mr. Calio previously served as a Managing Director within Energy and Infrastructure Investment Banking at BTIG, LLC (“BTIG”). Prior to BTIG, Mr. Calio spent 14 years at Morgan Stanley, most recently as a Managing Director within Equity Research, covering U.S. exploration and production companies, refiners, and integrated oils. Earlier in Mr. Calio’s career, he held a role within the Energy Investment Banking division at Morgan Stanley and the Energy Proprietary Trading business at JP Morgan. Mr. Calio began his career as a Special Counsel for the Securities and Exchange Commission (the “SEC”). Mr. Calio earned a B.S. from Lehigh University, a J.D. from Widener University School of Law, and an LLM from Georgetown University Law Center. There are no arrangements or understandings between Mr. Calio and any other persons pursuant to which he was appointed President. There are also no family relationships between Mr. Calio and any director or executive officer of the Company, and Mr. Calio has no direct or indirect material interest in any transaction required to be disclosed pursuant to Item 404(a) of Regulation S-K. Appointment of Chief Commercial Officer Also effective on November 12, 2026, Jaime Gualy, the Company’s current Chief Operating Officer, will transition to the role of Chief Commercial Officer. In connection with Mr. Gualy’s transition, his responsibilities will be assumed by other members of the Company’s Operations team, with a majority of his responsibilities being assumed by David Seigler, Senior Vice President, Special Projects & Operations, and Ryan Considine, Executive Vice President, Strategic Engineering & Advanced Manufacturing. Mr. Seigler, 52, joined the Company in June 2026 as Senior Vice President, Special Projects and has served as the Company’s Senior Vice President, Special Projects & Operations since October 2026. Mr. Seigler is a construction executive with more than 25 years of experience and has led large-scale commercial, industrial, federal, and mission-critical programs, with a specialization in mechanical, electrical, and plumbing systems. Item 3.02. Unregistered Sales of Equity Securities. As previously disclosed, T1 Energy Inc. (the “Company”) entered into an intellectual property purchase agreement, dated as of July 28, 2026 (the “IP Purchase Agreement”), with Evervolt Green Energy Holding Pte, Ltd. (“Evervolt”) pursuant to which the Company purchased all of Evervolt’s right, title and interest in and to certain intellectual property and proprietary rights, and related rights, and certain other assets (collectively, the “Purchase Assets”). The Company entered into the IP Purchase Agreement following its exercise of a call option granted to the Company by Evervolt under a call option letter agreement, dated July 27, 2026, between the Company and Evervolt (the “Call Option Agreement”). The terms of the IP Purchase Agreement and the Call Option Agreement were previously disclosed in the Company’s Form 8-K filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission on July 28, 2026 (the “July 28 Form 8-K”). The aggregate purchase price for the Purchased Assets was $133.0 million (the “IP Purchase Price”), which is in addition to a $2.0 million option premium the Company paid in consideration for the grant of the call option. The IP Purchase Price was, or is, payable in four tranches as described in the July 28 Form 8-K. Each tranche of the IP Purchase Price was, or is, payable, at the Company’s election, (a) in cash, (b) by the issuance to Evervolt of a number of shares of the Company’s common stock, par value $0.01 per share (the “common stock”), determined as described in the July 28 Form 8-K or (c) any combination of the foregoing in such ratio as mutually agreed by the Company and Evervolt. To satisfy the $30.0 million third tranche of the IP Purchase Price on October 15, 2026, the Company elected to issue 9,962,645 shares of common stock to Evervolt (the “October 15 Consideration Shares”). However, as previously disclosed, the Company and Evervolt have agreed that the issuance of any shares of common stock in satisfaction of any payment of the IP Purchase Price will be deferred (in whole or in part) if such issuance would cause Evervolt to beneficially own more than 4.99% of the then outstanding shares of the common stock (the “Ownership Limitation”). The issuance of the October 15 Consideration Shares is currently deferred pursuant to the Ownership Limitation. As previously disclosed, the issuance of 2,246,377 shares of common stock was previously deferred pursuant to the Ownership Limitation in connection with the $25.0 million second tranche of the IP Purchase Price payable on September 30, 2026, which the Company elected to satisfy with the issuance of 7,246,377 shares of common stock. The issuance of any shares of common stock as payment of the IP Purchase Price have been, or will be, made without registration under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the “Securities Act”), in reliance upon the exemption from registration provided by Section 4(a)(2) of the Securities Act. 1 SIGNATURE Pursuan

Entry into a Material Definitive Agreement. Note Purchase Agreement On September 28, 2026, T1 Energy Inc. (the “Company”) entered into a note purchase agreement (the “Note Purchase Agreement”) with a qualified institutional buyer that is an existing shareholder of the Company and new convertible notes investor (the “Purchaser”) for the sale of an additional $50.0 million in aggregate principal amount of the Company’s 4.75% Convertible Senior notes due 2031 (the “Convertible Notes”). The closing of the private placement is expected to occur on September 30, 2026 (such date, the “Closing Date”), subject to customary closing conditions. The gross proceeds from the sale of the additional Convertible Notes are expected to be approximately $50.4 million (which is equal to the principal amount of the Convertible Notes plus accrued interest from July 31, 2026, the date on which the Existing Notes (as defined below) were originally issued), prior to deducting fees and expenses. The Company expects to use the net proceeds from the private placement for (i) construction and development of infrastructure and purchase of production line equipment relating to Phase 1 of its G2_Austin solar cell fab (“G2_Austin”) and (ii) general corporate purposes. The net proceeds of the private placement are intended as a bridge to a comprehensive financing solution, which includes a significant debt component, to fund the remaining capital expenditures for Phase 1 of G2_Austin that the Company continues to target. Subject to certain limitations, the Note Purchase Agreement provides the Purchaser with certain registration rights for the shares of the Company’s common stock issuable upon conversion of the Convertible Notes. The Note Purchase Agreement requires the Company to prepare and file a new registration statement, or a prospectus supplement to the prospectus that forms a part of an existing registration statement, with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the “SEC”) as soon as reasonably practicable but in no event later than 30 calendar days following the Closing Date to register the resale of the shares underlying the Convertible Notes. The Note Purchase Agreement otherwise contains representations and warranties, covenants and other terms customary for an offering of this type. The above description of the Note Purchase Agreement is a summary and is not complete. A copy of the form of Note Purchase Agreement is filed herewith as Exhibit 10.1 to this Current Report on Form 8-K, and is incorporated herein by reference, and the above summary is qualified by reference to the terms of the Note Purchase Agreement set forth in such exhibit. Item 3.02. Unregistered Sale of Securities. The Convertible Notes are being sold to the Purchaser in a private placement pursuant to an exemption from the registration requirements of the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the “Securities Act”) provided by Section 4(a)(2) of the Securities Act. The Company is relying on this exemption from registration based in part on representations made by the Purchaser in the Note Purchase Agreement. To the extent that any shares of the Company’s common stock are issued upon conversion of the Convertible Notes, they will be issued in transactions anticipated to be exempt from registration under the Securities Act by virtue of Section 3(a)(9) thereof because no commission or other remuneration is expected to be paid in connection with conversion of the Convertible Notes and any resulting issuance of shares of common stock. Initially, a maximum of 13,440,860 shares of the Company’s common stock may be issued upon conversion of the Convertible Notes based on the initial maximum conversion rate of 268.8172 shares of common stock per $1,000 principal amount of Convertible Notes, which is subject to customary anti-dilution adjustment provisions. On October 27, 2026, the Board of Directors (the “Board”) of Tronox Holdings plc (the “Company”) approved the appointment of Yasser Al-Daajani as a new member of the Board. Mr. Al-Daajani was nominated to the Board by Cristal International Holdings B.V. (“Cristal”) pursuant to the Shareholders Agreement dated as of April 10, 2019 among the Company, Cristal and the other parties thereto. The appointment of Mr. Al-Daajani was effective as of October 27, 2026. Yasser F. Al-Daajani has served as Executive Vice President, Petrochemicals of National Industrialization Company (Tasnee)(TADAWUL: 2060), one of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia’s leading industrial companies, since June 2025. In this role, he is responsible for Tasnee’s petrochemicals business, including manufacturing, marketing, sales and supply chain operations. Mr. Al-Daajani has more than 25 years of experience in the petrochemicals industry and has held various leadership positions at Tasnee, where he has led strategic, operational and commercial initiatives across the business. He also serves on the board of several petrochemical joint ventures affiliated with Tasnee, including Saudi Polyolefins Company, Saudi Ethylene and Polyethylene Company, and Saudi Acrylic Acid Company. Mr. Al-Daajani holds a Bachelor of Science degree in Chemical Engineering from King Fahd University of Petroleum & Minerals and is an alumni of the Harvard Business School’s Senior Executive Leadership Program. Mr. Al-Daajani will receive compensation consistent with the other non-employee directors of the Company. Pursuant to this program, Mr. Al-Daajani will receive an annual cash retainer of $100,000, payable quarterly in arrears. In addition, Mr. Al-Daajani is entitled to an annual equity grant of time-based restricted share units with a fair market value of $150,000. There are no arrangements between Mr. Al-Daajani and any other persons pursuant to which Mr. Al-Daajani was selected as a director. There are no related party transactions between the Company and Mr. Al-Daajani that would be required to be reported pursuant to Item 404(a) of Regulation S-K under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended. CYPH.headline: Cantor Fitzgerald Maintains Buy Rating and Raises Price Target for Cypherpunk Technologies
CYPH.summary: Cantor Fitzgerald analyst Nathan Frankovitz maintained an Overweight rating on Cypherpunk Technologies (CYPH) while increasing the price target to $5.00 from $4.90.

DWTX.headline: Dogwood Therapeutics Announces Positive Phase 2b Results for Halneuron® in Chemotherapy-Induced Neuropathic Pain
DWTX.summary: Dogwood Therapeutics reported that its Phase 2b trial of Halneuron® met its primary endpoint, showing statistically significant pain reduction in cancer survivors with chemotherapy-induced neuropathic pain.

KEEL.headline: Analyst Initiates Coverage on Keel Infrastructure Corp.
KEEL.summary: An analyst has initiated coverage on Keel Infrastructure Corp. with a neutral rating.

RCAT.headline: Red Cat Holdings Receives Army Innovation Award
RCAT.summary: Red Cat Holdings was one of five companies selected to receive a $150,000 innovation award following the Kinetic Reach 2026 event.

TROX.headline: Pomerantz LLP Investigates Tronox Holdings plc for Potential Securities Fraud
TROX.summary: Pomerantz LLP has launched an investigation into Tronox Holdings plc regarding potential securities fraud or unlawful business practices following reports of creditor engagement in debt negotiations.
